newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - low priced Tapis offered in Bangchak.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - low priced Tapis offered in Bangchak.

text.p: Asia's crude trading remained lacklustre as the market waited for August trading to begin, traders said on Tuesday.
Some Minas parcels heard traded for July, but were probably done sometime last week, traders said.
Two shosha heard sold a total of 300,000 barrels of July Minas to China at ICP +20/25, while a Minas equity producer sold 100,000 barrels to a Japanese refiner at similar levels.
July Bontang Mix was also heard sold by a western trader at ICP +15 to a US major, but could not be confirmed.
But the light crude market was still depressed.
Rumours circulated that two cargoes of Tapis were offered into the Bangchak August purchase tender at fixed levels below $19.00.
This would equate to around August APPI -50/60, traders said.
Qatar crude deals done at discounts under QGPC dominated the Middle East crude market.
Over two million barrels of Qatar Marine crude were heard done since Friday, mainly to three U.S. majors.
Exact levels of the deals could not be confirmed, but ranged between discounts of 43 to 50 under QGPC, or at Dubai flat.
August Qatar Land was heard sold by a shosha Monday at QGPC -38, with Lower Zakum rumoured sold by another shosha at ADNOC -35/40, but both may be partial cargoes, traders said.
A U.S. major was thought to be the buyer for both trades, but this could not be confirmed.
Traders said activity on the Oman and Abu Dhabi crude markets should pick up after the award of the Bangchak tender, but did not expect prices to firm with ample supplies available.
Murban offers into Bangchak were heard around Dubai +80, with Oman offers heard at single digit premiums over Dubai.
